title: Human cluster access: AKS vs EKS vs GKE
summary: All three use the cloud's identity system to authenticate people to the Kubernetes API, but they differ on where authorization lives: in cloud IAM, in Kubernetes RBAC, or both.

dimensions.label: Authentication
values: IAM identity via aws eks get-token (pre-signed STS call)

dimensions.label: Authorization lives in
values: Azure RBAC (with Azure RBAC for K8s) or Kubernetes RBAC with Entra groups
EKS access entries + access policies (or Kubernetes RBAC via mapped groups)
Cloud IAM AND Kubernetes RBAC (either one can allow)

dimensions.label: Namespace-level grants from cloud IAM
values: Yes: role assignment at namespace scope
Yes: access entry with namespace accessScope
No: IAM is project-level; use RoleBindings

dimensions.label: Groups as subjects
values: Map IAM roles to Kubernetes groups in the access entry

dimensions.label: Credential that bypasses all of it
values: Local admin account (--admin): disable local accounts
Cluster creator's implicit admin: disable bootstrap admin
Legacy client cert / basic auth (off by default)

notes: GKE's 'either one can allow' model is the one that most often surprises people: a project-level IAM role silently overrides careful namespace RBAC.
In all three, prefer group-based grants at namespace scope, and treat the bypass credential in the last row as break-glass only.
